extracted.intended_audience: documentary filmmakers applying to the Sundance Institute Documentary Fund (feature-length filmmakers worldwide)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and eligibility criteria for applying to the Sundance Institute Documentary Fund, which supports feature-length nonfiction films at any stage (development through release). Covers eligibility, funding priorities, evaluation criteria, and procedural policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported formats / running time
rubrics_metrics.description: We support feature documentary films (52 minutes and longer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fund explicitly targets feature-length documentaries; shorter works are not listed as supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget priority
rubrics_metrics.description: We prioritize budgets under $1.2 million USD excluding distribution and impact expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with budgets below this threshold are prioritized; the budget figure is exclusive of distribution and impact spending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative and editorial control
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure the artist’s vision remains central, creative and editorial control must be held by the project’s key creative team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control must reside with the filmmakers/creative team — this is an eligibility/requirement intended to protect artistic authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior funding / fiscal sponsor not required
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior funding or a fiscal sponsor is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are not excluded for lack of previous funding or a fiscal sponsor — the Fund accepts projects without these in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: No resubmissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to the significant volume of applications we receive, we are unable to accept resubmissions for previously reviewed projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions are made only if a filmmaker has received a formal written invitation from the Sundance Institute Documentary Film Program staff to reapply; applicants are encouraged to consult the FAQ for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated for strong artistic vision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund values work that 'expresses the world in creative, complex, beautiful, and provocative ways.' Artistic vision is a core evaluation dimension, not a simple checkbox.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative ambition and craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated for creative ambition and craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment includes how the project demonstrates ambition in form and high craft in execution (cinematic qualities, storytelling, technical skill).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability and rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated for accountability and rigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This covers the project’s planning, ethical standards, feasibility, and seriousness of approach to production and subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contemporary cultural relevance and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated for contemporary cultural relevance and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund looks for projects with potential to generate social impact around compelling issues and that meaningfully engage cultural conversations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate and advance cultural dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Committed to nonfiction projects that elevate and advance cultural dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should contribute to deeper or broader public conversations; this is part of the Fund’s mission-driven evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand the form through creativity and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Committed to projects that expand the documentary form through creativity and innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for work that experiments with or broadens cinematic documentary language and approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential to generate social impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for projects that have the potential to generate social impact around some of the most compelling issues of our time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact can be thematic, community-oriented, policy-related, or cultural; Fund seeks projects with measurable or plausible impact pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct vision and meaningful connection to the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: We seek to uplift projects from filmmakers with distinct visions and meaningful connections to the work they create.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors filmmakers whose personal, cultural, or experiential connection to the subject strengthens the project’s authenticity and perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to diversity and global scope
rubrics_metrics.description: We remain committed to elevating voices beyond our borders and celebrating the rich diversity of filmmaking traditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund explicitly supports filmmakers worldwide and prioritizes diverse storytelling traditions and underrepresented voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support across project stages
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sundance Institute Documentary Fund supports filmmakers of cinematic documentaries worldwide, from development through release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants at any stage—development, production, postproduction, or release—may be considered; the Fund funds projects throughout the lifecycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonrecoupable funding model
rubrics_metrics.description: For over two decades, the fund has been a stable source of nonrecoupable funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants are not expected to be repaid to the Fund (nonrecoupable), affecting financial planning and reporting expectations.
